points.text: A·Ā = 0 (complement law: a variable ANDed with its complement is always 0).

questions.question: Q: How many cells does a 3-variable Karnaugh map have?
Q: On a K-map, what is the rule for grouping cells?

points.text: Groups must contain 1, 2, 4 or 8 adjacent cells in powers of two, and adjacent cells must differ by only one variable (Gray code ordering).

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: De Morgan's laws state: (1) (A·B)' = A' + B' — the complement of an AND is the OR of the complements; (2) (A + B)' = A'·B' — the complement of an OR is the AND of the complements. To convert an AND-OR circuit (implementing a Sum of Products expression F = A·B + C·D) to NAND-only, note that a NAND gate with both inputs tied together acts as a NOT gate. The expression F = A·B + C·D can be double-complemented: F = ((A·B + C·D)')'. By De Morgan's first law, the inner complement becomes (A·B)' · (C·D)'. So F = ((A·B)' · (C·D)')'. This requires only NAND gates: two NAND gates compute (A·B)' and (C·D)', and a third NAND gate combines them as ((A·B)' · (C·D)')'. Thus any SoP expression can be implemented entirely with NAND gates by double-complementing and applying De Morgan's laws.
